paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take from Titus 1. Church leadership is about who a man is, not how good he looks on Sunday. Paul says an elder must be "blameless," and he checks the home, the temper, the money, and the self-control (Titus 1:6-8). Nobody gets to be a different person at the front door than at the pulpit, and I once yelled at an oven timer, so I'm taking notes too.

Why does Paul care so much? Because the truth is worth protecting. An overseer must "hold firmly to the faithful word as it was taught," so he can encourage others with sound teaching and refute those who contradict it (Titus 1:9). Paul says empty talk and deception were undermining entire households, and that is why he wanted men in place who stand on God's word (Titus 1:10-11). That word rests on a promise from God, who "cannot lie," made before time began (Titus 1:2).

So here's the question for you, baker. Does my life match my words? Paul says some "profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him" (Titus 1:16). Saying you know God is easy, but living like it takes a heart He has made pure, and He is able to do that work. Let His word shape your actions today, and let your actions say what your mouth says.
